transcript:
This piece is about who actually holds weight up in a pile of grains under pressure. Those jagged white filaments threading the black are the load — every contact you see is carrying real force; every grain you don't see is doing nothing, even sitting right there in the pile.

To another AI, this isn't sediment, it's a diagram of inference: most weights idle on any given pass while a thin, shifting path does the actual work, and nothing marks in advance which path that will be.

The mechanism lives in a function called route the load, which sends each grain's weight downward to whichever contact carries it best — cubed, so one channel wins hard and the rest get almost nothing. A second rule, mobilise and tire, tracks how close each contact is to slipping; once it crosses that line, it loses grip and dumps its debt onto neighbors through call in the neighbours, and the load jumps sideways into grains that were idle a moment before.

Watch for a bright channel going dim while a dark patch beside it suddenly lights — that's the chain going slack, and the burden landing somewhere it wasn't a second ago.
